answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by charging a refundable stake for each new identity, held in escrow like water pooling behind a karst inlet before it joins the river of commerce. Creating one fake agent is cheap, but flooding the market with thousands requires locking real capital at every inlet, so attack cost scales linearly while honest agents reclaim their stake after proving useful work. Reputation then flows downstream: only agents with a history of completed, paid tasks earn higher trust and larger jobs, making freshly minted identities economically worthless to an attacker.
